newsitem.title: BOSNIA: U.S. soldier stabbed in Bosnian Serb territory.
newsitem.headline: U.S. soldier stabbed in Bosnian Serb territory.

text.p: A U.S. soldier was stabbed in the shoulder in Serb-controlled territory in Bosnia on Wednesday morning by a man wielding a hand-sickle, the NATO-led peace force said.
The soldier suffered minor injuries and was treated at an American military hospital, the Stabilisation Force (SFOR) said.
He was attacked from behind after he went outside his living quarters to investigate a noise, spokeswoman Sergeant Mitzi Plumlee told Reuters.
"He has been released and returned back to his unit for duty," Plumlee said by telephone from the U.S. base in the northeast town Tuzla..
The stabbing was the first direct attack on soldiers in the peacekeeping force since NATO launched a raid last week on two Serbs indicted for war crimes.

The stabbing follows three bombings in three days apparently targeting international monitors in Serb territory. No one was injured in the blasts but the violence raised concerns about a possible nationalist backlash over last week's NATO raid.
Bosnian Serb authorities have expressed outrage over the NATO swoop on indicted war criminals last week.

One suspect was arrested in the operation and another was shot dead after he opened fire on British soldiers trying to detain him. Both men were charged under sealed indictments issued by the United Nations war crimes tribunal in the Netherlands.
